A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAFE framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original proof-generation experiments on VerusBench and CodeNet-Test, synthesized-data statistics, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds sampling-budget comparisons, specification-score distributions, and DeepSeekCoder-1.3B experiments.

M1.justification: The translation, specification filtering, iterative fine-tuning, proof generation, and self-debugging procedures remain unchanged. The new loss equations document the existing training tasks. The inclusive filtering thresholds in v2 already appear in v1 Appendix C.1.

E1.justification: Both use MBPP and CodeNet for synthesis and evaluate on the same 139-task VerusBench and 1,435-task CodeNet-Test. The added smaller-model experiment and specification analysis introduce no new task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds previously absent raw GPT-4o, prompted GPT-4o, raw LLaMa, and raw DeepSeekCoder results to the VerusBench @100 comparison. Table 8 includes a raw DeepSeekCoder-1.3B reference. Renaming SAFE0 to Prompt does not itself change the comparator.

E3.justification: The central evaluation substantially revises sampling-budget accounting: Table 1 moves SAFE+ results formerly labeled @1 and @10 to @2 and @100, and adds two-generation controls. Its @100 SAFE+ setting explicitly uses 10 initial plus 100 debugging attempts. Appendix E.4 additionally evaluates a 1.3B backbone. These are reported evaluation changes, not evidence that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused checks of debugging versus independent generation at two attempts, specification correctness/completeness distributions in Figure 4, and self-evolution with a smaller backbone in Table 8. Existing decoding analyses, specification-quality ablations, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The paired t-test practice and p-values in Tables 5–7 are retained. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or another uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include two-attempt comparisons and baseline @100 scores in Table 1, specification distributions in Figure 4, and the complete 1.3B evolution results in Table 8. For example, its direct-generation Accuracy@10 rises from 6.47% raw to 40.29% after round 3. Retained SAFE+ scores such as 70.50% receive different budget labels; this is not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 newly defines the conditional negative-log-likelihood objectives for proof generation and debugging in Equations 2–3. This is limited mathematical formalization, with no new theorem or proof. Equation 1 merely expresses the previously described specification metrics as formulas.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains self-evolving proof generation under data scarcity. The abstract changes its headline comparison from 70.50% versus 24.46% to 52.52% versus 14.39%, reflecting different attempt budgets. The introduction also drops the broad extrapolation to any LLM and other formal languages.

C2.justification: New Appendix D discusses cross-function dependencies as an obstacle to large-project verification and proposes error-specific training edits to improve repeated debugging. Section 2.2 further explains why whole-proof debugging suits SMT-based verification. The existing failure example is retained in Appendix F.3, rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents training losses but omits v1's cap of ten incorrect proofs sharing an error and its estimate of three experts spending 40 hours on prompts. The promise to release code and benchmarks is also omitted. Appendix C.3's epochs, batch size, and learning rate remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning relative to expert iteration and SMT-based verification, adds references on specification evaluation and self-debugging, and removes several testing-oriented references from the introduction. The underlying positioning as applying self-evolution to data-scarce Rust verification remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and background undergo substantial rewriting, and proof-synthesis training is reorganized into two explicit tasks. Experiment subsections are restructured, specification examples move to the appendix, and the appendices gain a contents page and separate discussion, experiments, and case-study sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 and Table 8, expands Table 1, clarifies debugging-budget headers, and simplifies Table 3 by removing delta rows. Several displays move or resize, while the existing framework diagram, decoding plots, benchmark-distribution plots, and appendix proof listings remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: The new two-attempt controls strengthen evidence for self-debugging, while the smaller-model experiment and explicit scalability limitations improve support and qualification. Gains are limited by removed implementation details and inconsistent budget reporting: Table 1 labels 10 initial plus 100 debugging attempts @100, while Table 5 and Appendix F.3 retain earlier conventions. Overall, the evidence and explanations improve modestly.
